importance_ranking.reason: Extreme visual variation across sub-types — barracks, bunkers, command posts, hangars, and watchtowers are visually completely distinct structures. Buyers use the image to identify the product type before reading any text; wrong type is an immediate skip.

Shelter type, protection level, mobility, insulation, and climate zone are hard shortlisting gates for defence procurement. Without spec match, a listing cannot be evaluated for tender eligibility or operational fit.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall — market is fragmented across MES-registered approved vendors; buyers search by vendor registration status and DGQA approval, not manufacturer brand name.
importance_ranking.reason: MES vendor registration and DGQA approval are regulatory prerequisites for defence supply — an unregistered supplier with matching specs cannot be awarded a contract. Supplier qualification is a hard gate evaluated before price.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Containerised and inflatable shelter sub-segments quote per unit/per set — buyers must see the quoting basis to interpret any reference or indicative price correctly.
importance_ranking.reason: Per sq ft (custom panel shelters) vs per unit (containerised/inflatable) is a documented sub-segment ambiguity; the quoting basis must be visible for any indicative price to be interpretable.
Every sale is tender-quoted and negotiated through MES or command HQ procurement channels; listed price is a budget entry point only and is never the final transaction price.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines the primary product class — containerised, portable, fixed, and vehicle-mounted are non-interchangeable solutions with the largest price delta across all spec dimensions.

CBRN and ballistic protection require specialised manufacturing and carry a 3–5x price premium over weatherproof; entire procurement categories mandate specific protection levels as a compliance requirement.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Shelter size in sq ft is the primary cost driver for custom panel shelters and the dominant quoting basis in Indian defence procurement — without it, sellers cannot provide accurate indicative pricing.

PUF panel thickness (60mm to 120mm) is a standard configurator in Indian prefab defence shelters that drives insulation performance, structural load rating, and price — distinct from Insulation Type which captures material only.

Defence shelters at high-altitude and border locations must meet specific structural load and wind speed ratings as a procurement specification requirement — absent from the current spec list entirely.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Routes the RFQ to sellers who manufacture the specific shelter type — a barracks supplier cannot supply an aircraft hangar, making application the primary seller-routing spec.
Determines the structural and logistical solution class — a rapid deployable requirement cannot be met by a semi-permanent structure, so sellers need this to confirm product fit before responding.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need the required protection level to confirm manufacturing capability — a supplier without CBRN or ballistic production capability cannot respond to those requirements regardless of other spec matches.
